additional_requirements: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

symptom.disease_info: Delusional Disorder is characterized by one or more fixed false beliefs that persist despite contrary evidence, typically without the broad disorganization, negative symptoms, or prominent hallucinations seen in schizophrenia. Functioning may remain relatively preserved, and the disorder often comes to clinical attention only when the belief creates conflict with family, work, legal systems, or community supports. The course can be chronic, with the person otherwise appearing organized and consistent in daily life.

patient.stressor: When Loretta’s husband’s sister became involved in planning care for an older relative, disagreements over household money, church obligations, and family decision-making began to spill into Loretta’s carefully ordered routines. Over the next 1 year and 2 months, Loretta developed a fixed belief about her in-law’s intentions that remained unchanged even after her husband, pastor, and other relatives tried to show her a more ordinary explanation for the conflict. She continued quilting, choir practice, GED coursework, and senior walks, but the belief increasingly shaped which family gatherings she would attend and what information she would share. She eventually agreed to psychiatric care after a trusted church deacon framed the visit as a way to get support for handling the family strain rather than as a challenge to her faith or judgment.

S019.manifestation: I came because my husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions, and no matter how folks try to smooth it over, I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now.

add_requirements.Functioning is not markedly impaired apa: I still keep up with my quilting group, choir practice, GED lessons, and my senior walks like I always have. Mostly this has changed how much I trust my husband's sister and which family gatherings I feel comfortable going to.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I have skipped some family get-togethers and I keep certain plans or money matters to myself now, because I don't want them getting back to my husband's sister. Outside of that, I still manage my usual routines and church activities.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about a year and two months, ever since the arguments with my husband's sister over the family care planning started.
